name: Corona Pole Clip Spring
title: Corona Pole Clip Spring: Replacement Part
meta: Corona pole clip spring, a small replacement part that keeps the clip on a Corona pole snapping shut so sections and heads stay locked during pruning work.
tagline: A small replacement spring that brings a weak Corona pole clip back to a firm snap.
summary: The Corona pole clip spring is the small spring that keeps the locking clip on a Corona pole pressed into place. When the clip gets lazy and sections start to slip, a new spring is a cheap fix that puts the pole back to work.
highlights: Replacement spring for the clip on Corona poles
Restores firm lock-up between pole parts
Cheap fix compared with a new pole section
Worth keeping a spare in the truck kit
specs: Corona poles with a spring-loaded clip; confirm against your pole

p: Pole pruners and pole saws take a beating. They get dropped off the truck, dragged through brush and left out in the rain. The clip spring is one of the first parts to lose tension or rust through, and once it goes the clip no longer snaps home. That means a head or section that can twist or pull loose when you are working overhead.

Swapping the spring is usually a five-minute job with a small screwdriver or punch. Check the clip itself while it is apart. If the button or housing is cracked or worn, replace that too rather than trusting a new spring to make up for it.

If you run a crew, it pays to check every pole in the truck at the start of the season. Lock each section, give it a firm twist and a pull, and set aside any pole with a clip that does not seat. A bag of spare springs and a punch in the parts box means a pole can be fixed at lunch instead of going back to the shop.

Wipe sap and grit off pole joints at the end of the day and let them dry before storing. A light spray of dry lube on the clip helps keep it moving in winter. Never work a pole near energized lines unless it is rated for it and you are qualified for that work. For other small replacement parts, see our parts section.

faq.q: How do I know if I need a new pole clip spring?
faq.a: If the clip no longer snaps back on its own or the pole sections wiggle and slip when locked, the spring has likely lost tension or broken.

faq.q: Will this spring fit any pole?
faq.a: It is meant for Corona poles. Check the part against your pole model or the old spring before you order.

name: Husqvarna Chainsaw Maintenance Kit for 135, 435 and 440
title: Husqvarna Chainsaw Maintenance Kit for 135, 435, 440
meta: Husqvarna chainsaw maintenance kit for the 135, 435 and 440. Common wear parts in one pack for a season tune-up so the saw starts easy and runs clean all year.
tagline: Common wear parts in one pack for tuning up a Husqvarna 135, 435 or 440.
summary: This Husqvarna chainsaw maintenance kit bundles the common wear parts for the 135, 435 and 440 so a tune-up is one order instead of three. It is the easy way to keep a ground saw or firewood saw starting and running right.
highlights: Made for the Husqvarna 135, 435 and 440
Common service parts in a single pack
Good for an annual or end-of-season tune-up
Helps hard starting and rough running caused by worn filters and plugs
Check the listed contents against your saw

p: These are mid-size homeowner and light-duty saws, and on a tree crew they usually end up as the brush-cutting or bucking saw that never gets babied. A clogged air filter, a fouled plug or a dirty fuel filter will make any of them hard to start, bog under load and run hot. Replacing those parts together is cheaper than chasing one symptom at a time.

Check the kit's listed contents before you start so you know which parts you are swapping. Work on a clean bench, keep debris out of the intake while the filter is off, and gap or seat parts to the owner's manual.

A saw that has been sitting all winter often needs more than fresh fuel. Pull the plug and look at it: a black, sooty tip points to a rich mix or a dirty air filter, while a white, blistered tip can mean the saw is running lean and hot. Either way, fresh parts are the first step before anyone touches the carburetor.

Blow out the air filter at every few fills, use fresh fuel mixed at the ratio in the manual, and empty the tank before the saw sits for long. Keep the bar groove and oil hole clean so the chain gets oil. Always run the saw with the chain brake working and wear chaps, eye and ear protection, gloves and a helmet. More service parts are in our power equipment parts section.

faq.q: How often should I use a maintenance kit on my 435 or 440?
faq.a: Most owners do a full filter and plug change once a season, or sooner if the saw is used hard or in dusty conditions.

faq.q: Will this kit fit other Husqvarna models?
faq.a: It is listed for the 135, 435 and 440. Check part numbers before using it on any other model.

name: Husqvarna Clutch Cover for T540i XP
title: Husqvarna T540i XP Clutch Cover: Replacement Part
meta: Replacement Husqvarna T540i XP clutch cover for the battery top-handle saw. Swap a cracked or worn cover and get your climbing saw back into the tree quickly.
tagline: Replacement drive-side cover for the Husqvarna T540i XP battery top-handle saw.
summary: The Husqvarna T540i XP clutch cover is the drive-side cover that holds the bar and covers the sprocket on Husqvarna's battery top-handle saw. Replace it when the cover is cracked, the studs strip it or the chain catcher area is chewed up.
highlights: Replacement side cover for the Husqvarna T540i XP
Covers the drive sprocket and clamps the bar
Fixes cracked or worn covers that no longer hold tension
Keeps a working climbing saw in service

p: On a top-handle the side cover gets knocked against limbs, dropped on the lanyard and cranked down over and over at every bar change. A cracked cover, worn bar-nut seats or a damaged tension area means the bar can creep and the chain goes loose mid-cut. That is a problem on any saw, and a bigger one when you are working off a rope.

Even though the T540i XP is battery powered, the side cover is called the clutch cover by most parts lists. Pull the battery before any work on the saw, clean packed chips out of the sprocket area, then fit the new cover and tension the chain to spec.

Battery saws pack chips into the sprocket area just like gas saws, and on a climbing saw that mess often goes unnoticed until the chain starts to bind. Pop the cover off at the end of the day and brush the area out. That is also a good time to look at the bar rails and sprocket, since a worn sprocket wears new chain quickly.

Top-handle saws are for trained climbers working aloft. Tie the saw in to a saw lanyard, keep the chain brake working and tension the chain at every battery swap. Check the bar nuts are tight before you go back up. Find more service parts in our parts section.

faq.q: Does this fit the gas T540 XP?
faq.a: No. This cover is for the battery T540i XP. The gas T540 XP uses different parts.

faq.q: Do I need special tools to swap it?
faq.a: A scrench is usually all it takes. Remove the battery first and check that the bar and chain are seated correctly before tightening.

name: Husqvarna Replacement Hand Guard for 562XP
title: Husqvarna 562XP Hand Guard: Replacement Part
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 562XP hand guard. The front guard protects your hand and activates the chain brake, so replace it as soon as it is cracked or loose.
tagline: Front hand guard for the Husqvarna 562XP, a key part of the chain brake.
summary: The Husqvarna 562XP hand guard is the front guard that protects your left hand and trips the chain brake. If it is cracked, bent or loose on the saw, replace it before the next cut.
highlights: Front hand guard for the Husqvarna 562XP
Protects the front hand and works the chain brake
Replace cracked, broken or sloppy guards right away
Keeps a ground saw safe and compliant to run

body.h: A safety part, not a cosmetic one
p: The hand guard on a 562XP does two jobs. It shields your front hand from the chain and from branches, and it is the lever that applies the chain brake, either when you push it forward or, on many saws, by inertia in a kickback. A guard that is cracked or wobbly may not trip the brake the way it should.

Saws on a tree crew get thrown in the truck, dropped from the chipper and run into stumps. Check the guard and brake every morning: with the saw idling on the ground, engage the brake and confirm the chain stops. If the guard is damaged or the brake is slow, fix it before using the saw.

Hand guards usually break from impact rather than wear. A saw that slides off the tailgate, gets pinched in a cut and wrenched free, or takes a hit from a falling limb can crack the guard without anyone noticing. Make a quick look at the guard part of the morning saw check, along with the chain catcher and throttle lockout.

Follow the Husqvarna service steps or have a qualified shop fit it, since the guard connects to the brake mechanism. After fitting, test the brake several times before cutting. Never run a saw with a broken guard or a disabled brake. More service parts are in our power equipment parts section.

faq.q: Can I run my 562XP with a cracked hand guard?
faq.a: No. The guard is part of the chain brake system. Replace it and test the brake before using the saw.

faq.q: Does this fit the 562XP Mark II?
faq.a: Check the part number for your exact model. Mark II saws can use different parts from the original 562XP.

name: Husqvarna Starter Pulley Assembly for 562XP Mark II
title: Husqvarna 562XP Mark II Starter Pulley Assembly
h1: Husqvarna 562XP Mark II Starter Pulley Assembly
meta: Husqvarna 562XP Mark II starter pulley assembly. Replace a cracked or worn recoil pulley and get a reliable pull start back on your saw before the next job.
tagline: Recoil starter pulley for the Husqvarna 562XP Mark II.
summary: The Husqvarna 562XP Mark II starter pulley assembly is the rope pulley inside the recoil starter. When the cord will not rewind, slips or the pulley is cracked, this is the part that gets the saw pull-starting again.
highlights: Recoil starter pulley for the 562XP Mark II
Fixes slipping, binding or non-rewinding starters
Replace with a new starter cord at the same time
Keeps a working ground saw out of the shop

p: Starter pulleys wear at the pawl engagement and the rope channel, and they crack when the cord is yanked out to its end over and over. Symptoms are a cord that will not retract, a starter that spins without turning the engine, or a grinding feel on the pull. If the pulley is cracked, a new cord alone will not fix it.
While the starter housing is off, check the recoil spring, the pawls on the flywheel and the cord. Most people fit a fresh cord with the new pulley since the housing is already apart.

A failing starter is more than an annoyance on a busy day. Saws that do not start cleanly get yanked harder, drop-started and pulled at awkward angles, which is how people get hurt. A fresh pulley and cord brings back a smooth, predictable pull so the saw can be started properly on the ground with the brake on.

Recoil springs are under tension, so wear eye protection and gloves when the starter is apart and follow the service manual steps. Pre-tension the pulley the right number of turns so the handle returns firmly to the housing. On the job, start the saw on the ground with the brake on and avoid pulling the cord to its full length. For more service items browse our parts section.

faq.q: Will this pulley fit the original 562XP?
faq.a: It is listed for the 562XP Mark II. Check the part number before using it on an earlier 562XP.

faq.q: Should I replace the starter cord too?
faq.a: It is a good idea. The housing is already apart and a worn cord is the next thing to fail.

name: Spring Cassette Assembly for Husqvarna Chainsaw Recoil
title: Husqvarna Recoil Spring Cassette Assembly
meta: Husqvarna recoil spring cassette assembly for chainsaw starters. A pre-wound spring in its case makes fixing a starter that won't rewind quicker and safer.
tagline: Pre-wound recoil spring in a cassette for Husqvarna chainsaw starters.
summary: A Husqvarna recoil spring cassette puts the starter spring in its own case, so you swap one assembly instead of winding a loose spring by hand. It is the fix when the starter cord pulls out and will not come back.
highlights: Recoil spring held in a cassette
Faster and safer than winding a loose spring
Fixes cords that will not rewind
Fits Husqvarna starters built for a cassette spring; confirm your model
specs: Husqvarna chainsaw starters that use a cassette spring; confirm model

p: Many Husqvarna starters use a recoil spring housed in a plastic cassette. When the spring breaks or loses tension the cord stays out after a pull. A loose spring is fiddly and can uncoil fast, but a cassette drops in as one piece, which makes a field repair on the tailgate realistic.
Husqvarna has used different starter designs over the years, so match the cassette to your saw model or the old part before ordering. While the starter is apart, check the pulley and cord for wear.

Recoil springs fail most often in cold weather, when the spring steel is stiffer and the cord gets yanked to its full length. Get in the habit of pulling only until you feel compression, then giving a smooth, firm pull. Letting the handle snap back against the housing also stresses the spring, so guide it back in.

Wear eye protection and gloves when working on any recoil spring. Remove the starter housing, lift out the old cassette, seat the new one so it engages the pulley, then pre-tension the pulley as the manual says. Test that the handle returns snugly before refitting the housing. Start the saw on the ground with the chain brake on. Find more starter and service parts in our parts section.

faq.q: How do I know the spring is the problem?
faq.a: If the cord pulls out freely but does not rewind, or rewinds weakly, the recoil spring is the usual cause.

faq.q: Does it fit every Husqvarna saw?
faq.a: No. Starter designs vary by model, so check that your saw uses a cassette-type spring and match the part number.

h1: Westcoast Saw Clutch Cover for Husqvarna Chainsaws
meta: Westcoast Saw clutch cover for Husqvarna chainsaws, an aftermarket replacement side cover for climbers and ground crews. Confirm your saw model before ordering.
tagline: Aftermarket replacement clutch cover for Husqvarna saws from Westcoast Saw.
summary: The Westcoast Saw clutch cover for Husqvarna chainsaws is an aftermarket replacement for a cracked, worn or lost side cover. Westcoast Saw is known among arborists for parts and upgrades for the saws tree crews actually run.
highlights: Aftermarket clutch cover for Husqvarna saws
Replaces cracked or worn covers
From a maker focused on arborist saws
Check model fit before ordering

body.h: When the side cover needs replacing
p: The clutch cover clamps the bar and covers the clutch and sprocket. On tree saws it takes hits from limbs, gets dropped, and has its bar-nut seats crushed by years of cranking down with a scrench. Once it is cracked or the seats are worn, the bar can creep and chain tension will not hold.
This cover is a direct swap for the original part on the models it is listed for. Confirm your saw model before ordering, since Husqvarna covers differ between models and generations.

Aftermarket covers are popular with crews who would rather keep a spare in the truck than wait for a dealer order. If your crew runs a fleet of the same Husqvarna model, a spare cover in the parts box means a broken saw is back in service the same day.

Clean packed chips out of the clutch area, check the sprocket and clutch drum for wear, and confirm the chain catcher is in place. Fit the cover, tension the chain, then snug the bar nuts. Test the chain brake before cutting and wear full saw PPE. For more service parts see our parts section.
When ordering, have the saw's model and serial plate handy so the cover can be matched to the right version the first time.

faq.q: Which Husqvarna saws does it fit?
faq.a: Fit depends on the version. Check the model listing for this cover against your saw before buying.

faq.q: Does the cover include the chain brake?
faq.a: Check the listing. Some clutch covers include brake parts and some do not, and the brake must work correctly before the saw is used.

name: Westcoast Saw 3-Point Felling Dogs for Husqvarna Saws
title: Westcoast Saw 3-Point Felling Dogs for Husqvarna
h1: Westcoast Saw 3-Point Felling Dogs for Husqvarna Saws
meta: Westcoast Saw 3-point felling dogs for Husqvarna saws. Aggressive bucking spikes give a firm pivot in the wood for better control when felling and bucking.
tagline: Three-point bucking spikes for Husqvarna saws, for more bite when felling and bucking.
summary: Westcoast Saw 3-point felling dogs for Husqvarna saws replace the stock bumper spikes with a three-tooth dog that bites into the wood. A firm pivot point gives better control on face cuts, back cuts and bucking big wood.
highlights: Three-point felling dogs for Husqvarna saws
Firmer pivot in the wood than many stock spikes
Helps control on felling and bucking cuts
Bolt-on swap for the original dogs; confirm model

p: Felling dogs, or bucking spikes, give the saw something to pivot on. When you walk the saw through a big cut, a dog that grabs well lets you use leverage instead of pushing the bar into the wood. Stock spikes on some saws are short or blunt, and they slip on hard or frozen bark.
A 3-point dog has three teeth to set into the wood, which helps on removals, storm work and firewood when you are working near the full length of the bar.

Many sawyers also find better dogs help on smaller saws that are pushed into bigger wood than they were sold for. When the saw is near the end of its bar length, the ability to rock it on a solid pivot can make the difference between a clean cut and a pinched bar. Plan cuts so the bar is not trapped by compression wood.

Check the fit for your Husqvarna model, then swap the dogs with the bolts tight and the clutch cover refitted correctly. Keep the dogs sharp and free of chips. Felling dogs do not change the basics: plan the escape route, keep the chain brake working, and wear chaps, a helmet, eye and ear protection. Felling should only be done by trained operators. More saw parts are in our parts section.

faq.q: Do felling dogs make the saw cut faster?
faq.a: They do not change chain speed, but a firm pivot lets you use leverage on long cuts, which feels faster and easier.

faq.q: Will they fit my Husqvarna?
faq.a: Check the model list for this kit. Dog mounting differs between Husqvarna models.

name: Westcoast Saw 3-Point Felling Dogs for Stihl Chainsaws
keyword: westcoast saw 3-point felling dogs for stihl
title: Westcoast Saw 3-Point Felling Dogs for Stihl Saws
h1: Westcoast Saw 3-Point Felling Dogs for Stihl Chainsaws
meta: Westcoast Saw 3-point felling dogs for Stihl chainsaws. Bolt-on bucking spikes that grip the wood and give a steady pivot for felling cuts and big bucking.
tagline: Three-point bucking spikes for Stihl saws, for a steady pivot on big cuts.
summary: Westcoast Saw 3-point felling dogs for Stihl chainsaws give your saw a set of three-tooth spikes that dig into the wood. They make it easier to pivot the saw through felling cuts and long bucking cuts.
highlights: Three-point felling dogs for Stihl chainsaws
Bite into bark for a steady pivot point
Useful on removals, storm work and firewood
Bolt-on swap for the stock spikes; confirm model

p: When you set the dogs and walk the saw through the cut, the spikes act as the pivot. A dog that grips lets you lever the bar through the wood instead of forcing it, which saves your back on a long day of bucking. Smooth or worn spikes skip on hard bark and frozen wood.
The 3-point pattern gives three teeth to set, which is a common choice for sawyers running longer bars on big wood.

Stock bumper spikes on smaller Stihl models can be short, which limits how well the saw can pivot in big wood. A longer 3-point dog gives more bite and a more stable feel. Keep the dogs clear of debris and check the bolts after the first few hours of use, since vibration can loosen them.

Confirm the dogs are listed for your Stihl model, then fit them with the bolts snug and check that the clutch cover seats properly. Keep chips cleared from the dogs. Run the saw with a working chain brake and full PPE, and only fell trees you are trained and equipped to handle. Browse more saw parts in our parts section.
Some sawyers also like how a firm dog steadies the saw when making the hinge, though the hinge itself still has to be cut to the right size.

faq.q: Are these the same as the Husqvarna version?
faq.a: No. Mounting differs between brands, so buy the version made for your saw's brand and model.

faq.q: Do I need to remove the clutch cover to fit them?
faq.a: On most saws, yes. Check the bar and chain are seated and tensioned correctly after refitting.

name: Westcoast Saw Muffler for Echo CS-2511T
title: Echo CS-2511T Muffler by Westcoast Saw
h1: Echo CS-2511T Muffler by Westcoast Saw
meta: Echo CS-2511T muffler from Westcoast Saw. Replace a cracked, loose or carboned-up muffler and keep your small top-handle climbing saw running well.
tagline: Replacement muffler for the Echo CS-2511T, the small top-handle many climbers carry.
summary: This Echo CS-2511T muffler from Westcoast Saw replaces a damaged or worn muffler on Echo's small top-handle saw. It is a straightforward fix for a climbing saw that is running hot, loud or down on power.
highlights: Replacement muffler for the Echo CS-2511T
Swap a damaged, cracked or clogged muffler
From a maker focused on arborist top-handle saws
Check fit against your exact saw model

p: A muffler on a top-handle saw lives a hard life. It gets packed with sawdust and sap, bumped against the trunk and baked on long climbs. Cracked housings, broken mounts or a spark arrestor screen clogged with carbon will make the saw run hot, lose power and get louder.

The CS-2511T is light and quick, which is why so many climbers keep one on the saddle for pruning and small limbs. Keeping the exhaust in good shape is part of keeping that small engine healthy, along with clean filters and fresh, correctly mixed fuel.

Westcoast Saw is known for parts and modifications aimed at the top-handle saws climbers depend on. If the original muffler on your CS-2511T is cracked or loose at its mounts, a replacement is a quicker fix than waiting on a dealer order, and it gets the saw back on the saddle.

Let the saw cool before working near the muffler. Fit new gaskets if they are damaged, tighten the bolts evenly and check them again after the first tank. If your area or job needs a spark arrestor, make sure one is fitted. A change to exhaust flow can change how the saw runs, so have the carburetor checked if it is not idling or accelerating cleanly. Wear hearing protection whenever the saw is running. More top-handle parts are in our parts section.

faq.q: Will a new muffler change how the saw runs?
faq.a: It can. If the saw idles poorly or hesitates after the swap, have the carburetor adjusted by a qualified shop.

faq.q: Does this fit other Echo top-handles?
faq.a: It is listed for the CS-2511T. Check fit before using it on any other model.

name: 11/16 Ship Auger Bit
title: 11/16 Ship Auger Bit for Tree Cabling
meta: 11/16 ship auger bit for drilling clean, straight holes for tree cabling and bracing hardware. Single-flute design clears chips well in wet, green wood.
tagline: Ship auger bit for drilling clean holes for tree cabling and bracing hardware.
summary: This 11/16 ship auger bit (11/16 in.) drills the long, clean holes that cabling and bracing hardware needs. The single-flute design clears chips well in green wood, so the bit keeps cutting through thick limbs and stems.
highlights: 11/16 in. diameter ship auger bit
Single-flute design clears chips in green wood
Made for drilling cabling and bracing hardware holes
Runs in a heavy-duty drill or cordless drill with a suitable chuck
Pair the bit size with your hardware size
specs: Drilling holes for tree cabling and bracing hardware

p: Installing eye bolts, threaded rod and other through hardware means drilling straight, clean holes through living wood, often more than a foot deep. A ship auger has a single open flute and a lead screw that pulls the bit into the cut. It clears chips well in wet green wood where twist bits clog and bind.

This 11/16 in. bit is a common size for cabling work. ANSI A300 Part 3 sets out how holes should be sized relative to the hardware, and in general the hole should be only slightly larger than through hardware so it fits snugly. Check the standard and the hardware maker's instructions for the exact size.

Keep a sharp, straight bit in the cabling kit, and do not use the same bit for digging into soil or striking hardware. A bent or dull auger wanders, and a wandering hole leaves hardware off line from the cable, which is exactly what a good install avoids.

Drilling aloft puts a lot of torque on you and the drill. Use a drill with a side handle and clutch if you have one, secure your position with two points of attachment where required, and keep your lanyard and climbing line clear of the bit. Back the bit out often to clear chips, and keep the bit sharp so it does not stall. Cabling and bracing is structural work on a living tree. It should be specified and installed by a trained arborist following ANSI A300 Part 3, ANSI Z133 and the hardware maker's instructions, and inspected on a regular schedule after install. Shop hardware and tools in our cabling and bracing section.

faq.q: What size hardware is a 11/16 in. bit for?
faq.a: It depends on the hardware and the standard you follow. Check ANSI A300 Part 3 and the hardware maker's chart to match bit to hardware.

faq.q: Can I run a ship auger in a cordless drill?
faq.a: Yes, a strong cordless drill with a suitable chuck and side handle works. Larger bits need a high-torque drill and a firm stance.

name: 13/16 Ship Auger Bit
title: 13/16 Ship Auger Bit for Tree Cabling
meta: 13/16 ship auger bit for drilling clean, straight holes for tree cabling and bracing hardware. Single-flute design clears chips well in wet, green wood.
tagline: Ship auger bit for drilling clean holes for tree cabling and bracing hardware.
summary: This 13/16 ship auger bit (13/16 in.) drills the long, clean holes that cabling and bracing hardware needs. The single-flute design clears chips well in green wood, so the bit keeps cutting through thick limbs and stems.
highlights: 13/16 in. diameter ship auger bit
Single-flute design clears chips in green wood
Made for drilling cabling and bracing hardware holes
Runs in a heavy-duty drill or cordless drill with a suitable chuck
Pair the bit size with your hardware size
specs: Drilling holes for tree cabling and bracing hardware

p: Installing eye bolts, threaded rod and other through hardware means drilling straight, clean holes through living wood, often more than a foot deep. A ship auger has a single open flute and a lead screw that pulls the bit into the cut. It clears chips well in wet green wood where twist bits clog and bind.

This 13/16 in. bit suits larger through hardware. ANSI A300 Part 3 sets out how holes should be sized relative to the hardware, and in general the hole should be only slightly larger than through hardware so it fits snugly. Check the standard and the hardware maker's instructions for the exact size.

Larger bits demand more from the drill and the person running it. Use a drill that can handle the torque, keep both hands on it, and be ready for the bit to bind if it hits a knot or decay pocket. Back it out and clear chips rather than forcing it.

Drilling aloft puts a lot of torque on you and the drill. Use a drill with a side handle and clutch if you have one, secure your position with two points of attachment where required, and keep your lanyard and climbing line clear of the bit. Back the bit out often to clear chips, and keep the bit sharp so it does not stall. Cabling and bracing is structural work on a living tree. It should be specified and installed by a trained arborist following ANSI A300 Part 3, ANSI Z133 and the hardware maker's instructions, and inspected on a regular schedule after install. Shop hardware and tools in our cabling and bracing section.

faq.q: What size hardware is a 13/16 in. bit for?
faq.a: It depends on the hardware and the standard you follow. Check ANSI A300 Part 3 and the hardware maker's chart to match bit to hardware.

faq.q: Can I run a ship auger in a cordless drill?
faq.a: Yes, a strong cordless drill with a suitable chuck and side handle works. Larger bits need a high-torque drill and a firm stance.

name: Havens Grip Cable Puller
title: Havens Grip for Tensioning Tree Support Cable
meta: Havens grip for tensioning steel tree support cable. Clamps onto the strand so a come-along can pull it snug before you terminate it on cabling hardware.
tagline: Cable grip that clamps steel strand so you can pull it tight before terminating.
summary: A Havens grip clamps onto steel cable so you can pull the line snug with a come-along before you terminate it. In tree cabling it is the tool that takes up slack between anchors so the finished system sits at the right tension.
highlights: Clamps onto steel strand without a fixed end
Pairs with a come-along or hoist to pull cable
Grip tightens as load increases
Size the grip to the cable diameter you use
Inspect jaws for wear before every job

body.h: How it is used in cabling
p: When installing a static steel cable between two leaders, you anchor one end, run the cable to the second anchor and then need to take up slack before terminating. The Havens grip clamps onto the cable, a come-along hooks to the grip and the anchor, and you pull the leaders together just enough to remove slack, not to drag them into a new position.

Grip jaws are designed to bite harder as load increases, but they only work on the cable diameter range they are rated for. A grip that is too big will slip, and one that is too small will not close properly. Check the stamped size range and the working load against the job.

A Havens grip is also handy beyond cabling. Crews use come-along grips to snug guy lines and to hold cable while a second fitting is installed. Treat it as a tensioning tool with a rated capacity, and do not use it for lifting or for life support.

Keep the jaws clean of sap and grit and check the teeth for wear. Worn jaws can slip under load. Stay out of the line of pull when tensioning, since a slipping grip or failed cable can snap back. Cabling and bracing is structural work on a living tree. It should be specified and installed by a trained arborist following ANSI A300 Part 3, ANSI Z133 and the hardware maker's instructions, and inspected on a regular schedule after install. See more tools in our cabling and bracing section.

faq.q: What size Havens grip do I need?
faq.a: Match the grip's rated cable diameter range to the cable you are installing. The range is usually stamped on the grip.

faq.q: Can a Havens grip be left on the cable?
faq.a: No. It is a tensioning tool. Terminate the cable with the correct hardware and remove the grip.

name: HIT Cable Cutter
title: HIT Cable Cutter for Steel Tree Cabling Strand
meta: HIT cable cutter for trimming steel cable and strand cleanly during tree cabling installs. A compact hand tool for the cabling kit that saves time and fraying.
tagline: Hand cable cutter for clean cuts on steel strand during tree cabling jobs.
summary: The HIT cable cutter is a hand tool for cutting steel cable and strand cleanly, which is a regular job when installing tree support systems. A clean cut keeps the strand from unraveling and makes terminations neater.
highlights: Made for cutting steel cable and strand
Clean cut that limits fraying
Hand-powered, no blade to change
Check the rated cable size and type before cutting
A useful tool for every cabling kit
specs: Cutting steel cable and strand within its rated capacity

p: Cutting galvanized strand with bolt cutters or a grinder tends to crush and fray the end, and a grinder throws sparks and heat. A dedicated cable cutter has shaped jaws that shear the wires together, leaving an end that is easier to feed into grips and dead-ends.

Every cutter has a rated capacity, and some are not made for hardened steel such as high-strength strand. Check the tool's rated cable size and type before using it, and do not force it on cable beyond that rating, which can damage the jaws.

Keep the cutter in the cabling bag with the grips, dead-ends and thimbles, so everything needed to finish a run of cable is in one place. A cutter that lives in the truck tool box is a cutter that is not there when you are in the tree with a cable end to trim.

Tape the cable on both sides of the cut to keep it tidy, set the cable deep in the jaws and cut with a steady squeeze. Wear eye protection and gloves since cut strand ends are sharp. Keep the pivot clean and lightly oiled. Cabling and bracing is structural work on a living tree. It should be specified and installed by a trained arborist following ANSI A300 Part 3, ANSI Z133 and the hardware maker's instructions, and inspected on a regular schedule after install. Find more tools in our cabling and bracing section.

faq.q: Will it cut EHS strand?
faq.a: Only if the cutter is rated for it. Check the capacity and cable types listed for the model you have.

faq.q: How do I stop the cut end from fraying?
faq.a: Wrap tape on both sides of the cut point before cutting, and cut with the cable seated deep in the jaws.

name: Preformed Line Products Tree Cabling Lag Spinner
title: Preformed Line Products Lag Spinner for Tree Cabling
h1: Preformed Line Products Tree Cabling Lag Spinner
meta: Preformed Line Products lag spinner for tree cabling. A drill attachment that drives lag eye hardware into pilot holes faster and straighter than by hand.
tagline: Drill attachment for driving lag-type cabling hardware into the tree.
summary: The Preformed Line Products lag spinner lets you drive lag-type cabling hardware with a drill instead of cranking it in with a bar. It speeds up installs and helps set hardware to depth evenly.
highlights: Drives lag-type eye hardware with a drill
Faster than turning hardware in by hand
Helps set hardware straight and to depth
Pairs with a properly sized pilot hole
A handy addition to a cabling kit

p: Lag eyes and similar hardware are threaded into a pilot hole drilled into the leader. Turned by hand with a bar through the eye, it is slow and easy to wobble off line. A lag spinner fits the eye and is driven by a drill, so the hardware goes in steadily and straight.
Use a drill with a clutch or controlled speed so you can stop when the hardware reaches depth. Over-driving can strip the threads in the wood and weaken the hold.

A lag spinner is most useful on jobs with several anchors, such as multi-leader systems. Setting each lag at the same speed and depth helps keep the system consistent. Keep the spinner clean and check it for wear where it bears on the eye, since a worn spinner can slip and mark the hardware.

Drill the pilot hole to the size the hardware maker specifies for lags, keep the hardware in line with the cable direction, and stop when the eye is set. Drilling and driving aloft takes a solid position, so keep your climbing system clear of the drill and work with two points of attachment where required. Cabling and bracing is structural work on a living tree. It should be specified and installed by a trained arborist following ANSI A300 Part 3, ANSI Z133 and the hardware maker's instructions, and inspected on a regular schedule after install. See more in our cabling and bracing section.

faq.q: Can I use it with any drill?
faq.a: Use a drill with enough torque and a clutch or variable speed so you can control the final turns. Check the spinner's fit against the hardware you use.

faq.q: Is lag hardware right for every tree?
faq.a: No. Hardware type depends on the stem size, wood condition and system design. Follow ANSI A300 Part 3 and get a qualified arborist to specify the system.

name: Weaver Nylon Basket for Cable
title: Weaver Nylon Basket for Cable and Cabling Hardware
meta: Weaver nylon basket for cable that keeps a coil of tree support cable and hardware together for the climb. Clips to the saddle or hangs on a line in the canopy.
tagline: Nylon basket to carry tree cable and hardware up the tree.
summary: The Weaver nylon basket for cable gives you a place to carry a coil of support cable and hardware into the tree. Having everything in one basket at the work position saves trips and keeps parts from dropping to the ground.
highlights: Nylon basket for cable and cabling hardware
Keeps parts together at the work position
Can be sent up on a line or hung near the work
Durable nylon from a long-time arborist gear maker
specs: Carrying cable and cabling hardware aloft

body.h: Why a basket helps on cabling jobs
p: A cabling install means a coil of cable, grips, dead-ends, hardware, a drill and bits, all needed at the same spot high in the crown. Stuffing hardware in pockets is how parts end up in the lawn. A basket hung near the work position holds the coil and small parts so you can reach them without juggling.
Weaver has been making arborist gear for a long time, and this basket is made in tough nylon that stands up to cable ends and hardware better than a light bag.

Cable coils are springy and awkward, and cut strand ends are sharp. A basket with a stiff body holds the coil open so it does not unwind across your lap. Keep hand tools, such as the cable cutter and grips, in the basket too so you are not reaching for pockets while on rope.

Hang the basket from a dedicated attachment point, not from your life-support system, and keep it below the weight the basket and attachment are rated to hold. Keep the work zone below clear in case anything drops, and send heavy items up on a separate line. Inspect the stitching and handles before each job. Find more tools and hardware in our cabling and bracing section.

faq.q: Can I clip it to my saddle?
faq.a: Use a gear loop or a dedicated tool attachment, never your life-support connection points, and keep the load light.

faq.q: Will it hold a full coil of cable?
faq.a: It depends on the coil size. Check the basket's dimensions against the cable you carry.

name: 1/2 in. Turnbuckle
title: 1/2 Turnbuckle for Tree Cabling and Guying
meta: 1/2 turnbuckle in galvanized steel for adjusting tension in tree support and guying systems. Fine take-up adjustment once cable is set between two anchors.
tagline: A 1/2 in. turnbuckle for fine tension adjustment in guying and support systems.
summary: A 1/2 turnbuckle, meaning one with 1/2 in. threads, gives you fine tension adjustment in a steel cable or guying system. Turning the body draws the two ends together or lets them out, so slack can be taken up after the system is installed.
highlights: 1/2 in. thread size
Fine tension adjustment after installation
Used in guying and some support systems
Choose galvanized hardware for outdoor use
Check the rated working load for your system

p: Turnbuckles are used where a system needs to be adjusted after it is in place, such as guying a newly planted or leaning tree to a ground anchor. They are less common in modern static cabling between leaders, where cable is usually tensioned with a grip and come-along before termination.
Pick the end fittings (eye, hook or jaw) to suit the hardware they connect to. Hooks can open under shock load, so many installers prefer eye or jaw ends for anything structural.

Use galvanized hardware so the turnbuckle matches the rest of the system and resists rust outdoors. Check the turnbuckle's rated working load against the system design, and never use a turnbuckle as part of a life-support system or rigging setup.

Thread both ends in evenly so the turnbuckle has room to take up or let out. Lock the body with wire or a lock nut so it cannot back off with movement. Tension only enough to take out slack. Check the system on a regular schedule and adjust or remove guying when it is no longer needed. Cabling and bracing is structural work on a living tree. It should be specified and installed by a trained arborist following ANSI A300 Part 3, ANSI Z133 and the hardware maker's instructions, and inspected on a regular schedule after install. See more hardware in our cabling hardware section.

faq.q: Do I need a turnbuckle for tree cabling?
faq.a: Not usually for leader-to-leader cabling. They are more common in guying, where tension may need adjusting over time.

faq.q: How do I stop a turnbuckle loosening?
faq.a: Lock the body with safety wire or lock nuts after setting tension.

name: 5/8 in. Eye Bolt
title: 5/8 Eye Bolt for Tree Cabling Through Hardware
meta: 5/8 eye bolt, drop-forged, for through-bolt tree cabling and bracing anchors. Install with a washer and nut through the leader to the ANSI A300 standard.
tagline: A 5/8 in. eye bolt anchor for through-bolted tree cabling systems.
summary: A 5/8 eye bolt is a 5/8 in. diameter through-bolt anchor for tree cabling. It passes through the leader and is held with a washer and nut on the far side, giving the cable a strong attachment point.
highlights: 5/8 in. diameter through-bolt anchor
Drop-forged eye for cable attachment
Installed with washer and nut on the far side
Choose galvanized for outdoor durability
Select length to suit the stem diameter

p: Through hardware is the strong option in a cabling system. The eye bolt passes completely through the leader, so the load is shared by wood on both sides. A flat or beveled washer and nut on the far side seat the hardware against the bark, and the cable attaches to the eye.

Choose a length that passes through the stem with enough thread for the washer and nut. Drill the hole in line with the direction of the cable so the eye does not bend under load, and size the hole per ANSI A300 Part 3.

Through hardware such as a 5/8 eye bolt is common in cabling and in some bracing setups. Using the same diameter hardware throughout a system keeps the drill bits, washers and nuts consistent in the kit and makes it easier to inspect.

Use drop-forged, galvanized hardware rated for the job, and use a thimble where the cable passes through the eye. Do not set the eye deep into the wood or cut away bark to seat hardware. Inspect for corrosion, bending and wood decay around the hardware on a regular schedule. Cabling and bracing is structural work on a living tree. It should be specified and installed by a trained arborist following ANSI A300 Part 3, ANSI Z133 and the hardware maker's instructions, and inspected on a regular schedule after install. Find the rest of the system in our cabling hardware section.

faq.q: What size hole do I drill for a 5/8 eye bolt?
faq.a: Follow ANSI A300 Part 3 and the hardware maker's chart. Through-hardware holes are drilled only slightly larger than the bolt.

faq.q: Is through hardware better than lags?
faq.a: Through hardware is generally stronger and is often preferred where the stem size allows. The system designer should choose based on the tree.

name: Amon Eye Nut
title: Amon Eye Nut for Tree Cabling Threaded Rod
meta: Amon eye nut for tree cabling. It threads onto rod or a bolt end to give a forged eye for cable attachment, turning threaded rod into a strong through anchor.
tagline: A forged eye nut that turns threaded rod into a cable anchor point.
summary: An Amon eye nut threads onto threaded rod or a bolt end to give a forged eye for cable attachment. It is a classic way to build through-hardware anchors in tree cabling, cut to length on site.
highlights: Forged eye that threads onto rod
Builds a through anchor cut to stem length
Seats against a washer on the bark
Match the thread size to your rod
Galvanized for outdoor use
specs: Cable anchor on threaded rod or bolts

p: Eye bolts come in fixed lengths. With threaded rod and an Amon eye nut you can build an anchor to exactly the length a stem needs. The rod goes through the leader, a washer and the eye nut go on the cable side, and a washer and nut hold the far end.
Thread size must match the rod. Thread the eye nut on fully so it seats against the washer, and set the eye in line with the direction of the cable.

An eye nut on threaded rod also lets you fine-tune where the eye sits relative to the bark, which helps keep the eye close to the stem without being buried. Keep a mix of rod lengths and eye nuts in the kit so you are ready for stems of different sizes.

Use galvanized, forged hardware rated for the system, drill the hole per ANSI A300 Part 3, and fit a thimble where the cable runs through the eye. Trim excess rod so it does not stick out far. Inspect for corrosion and wood decay around the hardware over time. Cabling and bracing is structural work on a living tree. It should be specified and installed by a trained arborist following ANSI A300 Part 3, ANSI Z133 and the hardware maker's instructions, and inspected on a regular schedule after install. See more parts in our cabling hardware section.

faq.q: Is it spelled Amon or Ammon?
faq.a: Both spellings are used in catalogs. They refer to the same type of forged eye nut.

faq.q: What rod do I use with it?
faq.a: Galvanized threaded rod with a matching thread size, cut to suit the stem diameter.

name: Galvanized Flat Washer
title: Galvanized Flat Washer for Tree Cabling Hardware
meta: Galvanized flat washer for tree cabling and bracing hardware. It spreads nut and eye load across the wood and resists rust on hardware left in the tree.
tagline: Galvanized washers to seat nuts and eyes on through-bolted cabling hardware.
summary: A galvanized flat washer sits under the nut or eye of cabling and bracing hardware to spread the load over the wood. The galvanized finish holds up outdoors, which matters for hardware that stays in a tree for years.
highlights: Galvanized for outdoor use
Spreads nut and eye load over the wood
Used on through-bolted cabling and bracing
Match the hole size to your hardware
Keep a supply in the cabling kit

p: Through hardware needs something between the nut or eye and the tree. A washer spreads the clamping load so the nut does not crush into the bark and wood. On rounded stems, many installers use a beveled or curved washer where it seats better, and a flat washer where the surface allows.
Match the washer's hole to the hardware diameter. A washer with an oversized hole lets the nut pull into it and defeats the point.

Buy washers in quantity, since every through-bolt anchor needs at least one and they are easy to drop. Keeping a jar of matched washers and nuts for each hardware size in the cabling kit saves a lot of searching and makes sure the right parts go in the tree.

Seat the washer against the bark without cutting away more than needed, and snug the nut firmly. Mixed metals can corrode, so keep to galvanized hardware throughout the system. Check washers and nuts at each inspection for rust, loosening and wood growth over the hardware. Cabling and bracing is structural work on a living tree. It should be specified and installed by a trained arborist following ANSI A300 Part 3, ANSI Z133 and the hardware maker's instructions, and inspected on a regular schedule after install. See more in our cabling hardware section.

faq.q: Flat washer or beveled washer?
faq.a: Use whichever seats better on the stem. Beveled or curved washers suit rounded surfaces; flat washers suit flatter spots.

faq.q: Why galvanized?
faq.a: Cabling hardware stays outdoors for years. Galvanizing slows corrosion and matches other galvanized hardware in the system.

name: Preformed Line Products Dead-End Cable Grips
title: Preformed Line Products Dead-End Cable Grips
h1: Preformed Line Products Dead-End Cable Grips
meta: Preformed Line Products dead-end cable grips terminate steel strand by wrapping it with helical rods. A fast, tidy way to finish a tree cable at the anchor eye.
tagline: Helical dead-ends for fast, clean termination of steel support cable.
summary: Preformed Line Products dead-end cable grips terminate steel strand with helically formed rods that wrap around the cable. In tree cabling they make a quick, tidy termination at the anchor eye.
highlights: Helical-wrap termination for steel strand
Fast to install with no clamps or splices
Sized to a specific cable diameter
Widely used in utility and tree cabling
Use with a thimble at the anchor eye
specs: Match to cable diameter and type

p: A dead-end grip is a set of preformed helical rods. You loop it around a thimble in the anchor eye and wrap both legs onto the cable. The helix grips the strand along its length, spreading the load without clamps or hand splices.

Each grip is made for a specific cable diameter and type. A grip on the wrong size cable will not hold its rated load. Check the color code or marking on the grip against the cable you are installing.

Dead-end grips have become common in tree cabling because they are quick to install aloft and do not depend on the installer's splicing skill. They do still need to be applied correctly, so practice on the ground before using them in a tree.

Use a thimble at the eye, wrap the legs fully onto the cable and do not reuse grips once they have been applied and removed unless the maker allows it. Leave enough cable tail as the instructions show. Inspect at each check for corrosion, slipping and wear at the eye. Cabling and bracing is structural work on a living tree. It should be specified and installed by a trained arborist following ANSI A300 Part 3, ANSI Z133 and the hardware maker's instructions, and inspected on a regular schedule after install. Find the rest of the hardware in our cabling hardware section.

faq.q: Can I reuse a dead-end grip?
faq.a: Follow the maker's instructions. Many helical dead-ends are not meant to be reused after they have been removed.

faq.q: Do I need a thimble?
faq.a: Yes, a thimble at the anchor eye protects the grip and cable from a sharp bend and wear.

name: Rig Guy Beveled Washer
title: Rig Guy Beveled Washer for Tree Cabling
meta: Rig Guy beveled washer for tree cabling hardware. The angled face seats on the curved surface of a stem so nuts and eyes pull down evenly against the wood.
tagline: Beveled washer that seats cabling hardware evenly on a rounded stem.
summary: The Rig Guy beveled washer has an angled face that seats against the curve of a stem, so cabling hardware pulls down evenly. It helps hardware sit square to the load instead of rocking on a rounded surface.
highlights: Beveled face for rounded stems
Helps hardware seat square to the load
Spreads nut or eye load across the wood
Part of a matched cabling hardware system
Match hole size to your hardware
specs: Seating cabling hardware on rounded stems

p: Leaders are round, and a flat washer on a curved surface only touches in a couple of spots. That can let the nut bite into the bark or let the hardware cock to one side. A beveled washer seats better on the curve so the load is shared more evenly.
Match the washer to the hardware diameter and the rest of the Rig Guy parts you are using. Mixing systems can leave gaps or poor seating.

Washers that do not seat cleanly can let water collect and speed corrosion around the hardware. A beveled washer that fits the stem helps shed water and keeps the hardware tight, which helps the system last longer between inspections.

Seat the washer with the bevel matched to the stem, snug the nut firmly, and avoid cutting away bark to seat it. Check washers and nuts at each inspection for rust, loosening and wood growing over the hardware. Cabling and bracing is structural work on a living tree. It should be specified and installed by a trained arborist following ANSI A300 Part 3, ANSI Z133 and the hardware maker's instructions, and inspected on a regular schedule after install. See more in our cabling hardware section.

faq.q: When should I use a beveled washer instead of a flat one?
faq.a: Use a beveled washer where the stem curve would stop a flat washer from seating fully.

faq.q: Does it work with other brands of hardware?
faq.a: Check that the hole size and fit match your hardware. A matched system usually seats best.

name: Rig Guy Finishing Caps
title: Rig Guy Finishing Caps for Tree Cabling
meta: Rig Guy finishing caps cover cut cable ends and hardware on a finished tree cabling job. A tidy, professional finish that keeps strand ends from fraying.
tagline: Caps that finish off cable ends and hardware on a tree cabling install.
summary: Rig Guy finishing caps cover the ends of cable and hardware once a tree cabling system is installed. They give the job a clean finish and help keep cut strand ends from fraying or snagging.
highlights: Finishes cut cable ends and hardware
Helps stop strand ends fraying
Tidy, professional look on the finished job
Part of the Rig Guy cabling system
Match the cap to your cable or hardware size
specs: Covering cable ends and hardware on finished installs

p: A cut strand end left bare can unravel over time and snag a climber's rope or a hand during later inspections. A finishing cap covers the end so the system looks finished and the end stays tidy.
Caps are sized to the cable or hardware they cover. Match them to the parts you used for the install.

Finishing caps also make inspections easier, since a cap that is missing or damaged is a quick visual sign to look closer at that part of the system. Keep a few spares in the kit so caps lost during install can be replaced on the spot.

Fit caps after the system is tensioned and terminated. They are a finishing part, not a structural one, so never rely on a cap to hold anything. At each inspection, check that caps are still in place and that the hardware beneath is sound. Cabling and bracing is structural work on a living tree. It should be specified and installed by a trained arborist following ANSI A300 Part 3, ANSI Z133 and the hardware maker's instructions, and inspected on a regular schedule after install. See more parts in our cabling hardware section.
Order caps with the rest of the job's hardware so the install can be finished in one visit to the tree.

faq.q: Are finishing caps structural?
faq.a: No. They finish and protect the ends. The terminations carry the load.

faq.q: What size do I need?
faq.a: Match the cap to the cable or hardware size used in the install.

name: Rig Guy Wire Hub Stop
title: Rig Guy Wire Hub Stop for Tree Cabling
meta: Rig Guy wire hub stop, a fitting used in the Rig Guy tree cabling system to hold the wire in place at the hub. Check sizing against your cable first.
tagline: Stop fitting that holds the wire at the hub in a Rig Guy cabling system.
summary: The Rig Guy wire hub stop is a fitting used in the Rig Guy tree cabling system to hold the wire in position at the hub. It is one of the matched parts that keeps a multi-way installation set up the way it was designed.
highlights: Wire stop for Rig Guy hub systems
Holds cable position at the hub
Part of a matched cabling system
Size to the cable diameter used
specs: Holding wire position at a cabling hub

body.h: Where it fits in the system
p: Hub-style cabling links several leaders through a central point, which is common where a crown has three or more weak unions. Each wire needs to stay at its set position at the hub, and the stop fitting is what holds it there.
Use the stop with the cable diameter and hub it is made for. Mixing parts from different systems can let a wire slip or seat poorly.

Hub systems are often used where leaders need support in more than one direction. Because each wire relates to the others, a single stop that slips can change the load on the whole system, which is why careful setting and regular checks matter.

Follow the system maker's install steps for setting and securing the stop. Check each stop at inspection for slipping, corrosion and wear, and confirm the cable lengths have not changed. Cabling and bracing is structural work on a living tree. It should be specified and installed by a trained arborist following ANSI A300 Part 3, ANSI Z133 and the hardware maker's instructions, and inspected on a regular schedule after install. Browse the rest of the hardware in our cabling hardware section.
Record each wire's position and the stop locations at install, which makes later inspections quicker and more reliable.

faq.q: Can I use it with other cabling hardware?
faq.a: It is designed for Rig Guy hub systems. Check fit with the maker before mixing parts.

faq.q: How often should the system be inspected?
faq.a: Follow the schedule set by the arborist who designed the system; many recommend at least annual checks and after major storms.

name: Duckbill Drive Rod for Large Earth Anchors
title: Duckbill Drive Rod for Large Earth Anchors
h1: Duckbill Drive Rod (Large) for Earth Anchors
meta: Duckbill drive rod, large size, for setting the bigger Duckbill earth anchors used to guy newly planted trees. Drive the anchor to depth, pull the rod, lock.
tagline: Steel drive rod for setting the larger Duckbill earth anchors when guying trees.
summary: The large Duckbill drive rod is the steel rod used to drive the bigger Duckbill earth anchors into the ground for guying newly planted trees. Drive the anchor to depth, pull the rod, then load-lock the anchor.
highlights: Drive rod for larger Duckbill anchors
Sets anchors to depth without digging
Reusable steel rod
Used for guying new plantings
Check the rod matches your anchor model
specs: Larger Duckbill anchor models; confirm against your anchor

p: Duckbill anchors are driven into undisturbed soil with a drive rod and a hammer or driver. Once at depth, the rod is pulled out and the cable is pulled up, which rotates the anchor sideways into a locked position. It is much faster than digging in deadmen, and the hole is small.
Larger anchors need the larger rod. Check the rod against the anchor model before you start, since the wrong rod will not seat or drive the anchor properly.
Keep the drive rod straight and clean, and mark it at the target depth so the crew knows when the anchor is set. A bent rod can bind or fail to release the anchor, so check it before each job.

Locate buried utilities before driving anything into the ground. Drive anchors outside the root ball, at an angle away from the tree. Use soft, wide straps against the trunk so the guying does not girdle the bark, leave some movement so the tree builds strength, and remove the guying once the tree is established, often after one growing season. Wear eye protection and gloves when driving. Find more planting supplies in our planting section.
Choose anchors and rods rated for the size of the tree, and follow the anchor maker's instructions for depth and load-locking.

faq.q: Can I use the large rod on small Duckbill anchors?
faq.a: Use the rod size made for your anchor model. A mismatched rod may not seat the anchor.

faq.q: How long should a tree stay guyed?
faq.a: Usually only until it is rooted in, often one growing season. Check and remove guying promptly.

name: Corona Bull Tree Pruner Head
title: Corona Bull Tree Pruner Head for Pole Pruning
meta: Corona Bull tree pruner head, a rope-pull bypass pole pruner head for clean cuts on overhead branches from the ground. Mounts to a pole for reach and leverage.
tagline: Rope-operated pole pruner head for cutting overhead limbs from the ground.
summary: The Corona Bull tree pruner head is a rope-operated pole pruner head for cutting overhead branches from the ground. Mounted on a pole, it lets ground crews and climbers make clean cuts on small limbs without a saw.
highlights: Pole pruner head from Corona
Rope-pull action for overhead cuts
Clean bypass-style cuts on small limbs
Mounts to a pole; check fit to your pole
Replaceable head for a worn-out pruner

body.h: Where a pole pruner head earns its keep
p: A pole pruner head is the go-to for clearing small limbs overhead, lifting a canopy over a driveway or taking deadwood out of a small tree without climbing. Pulling the rope closes the blade, and the leverage built into the head does most of the work.
It is best on smaller-diameter live wood where a clean cut matters. For larger limbs, switch to a pole saw rather than forcing the pruner, which can bend the blade or crush the branch.

Pole pruner heads wear at the blade, the pivot and the rope pulley. When a head starts to mash branches rather than cut them, a new head is usually a better fix than fighting a worn one. Keep a spare rope on the truck too, since a frayed rope can snap mid-cut.

Stand to the side of the branch, not under it, and wear a helmet and eye protection. Never use a pole tool near power lines unless it is rated for that work and you are qualified. Keep the blade clean and sharp, oil the pivot, and check the rope for wear. Replace the rope or head when they are damaged. See more pruning tools in our pruners and loppers section.

faq.q: Will this head fit my pole?
faq.a: Check the mounting style against your pole before buying. Fit varies between pole systems.

faq.q: How big a branch can it cut?
faq.a: Check the stated capacity for the head and switch to a pole saw for anything larger.

name: Corona Bypass Pruner, 1 in. Capacity
title: Corona Bypass Pruner with 1 in. Cutting Capacity
meta: Corona bypass pruner with 1 in. cutting capacity for clean pruning cuts on live wood. A tough hand pruner sized for structural pruning and small-tree work.
tagline: Hand bypass pruner with 1 in. capacity for clean cuts on live wood.
summary: This Corona bypass pruner cuts branches up to 1 in. thick with a clean, scissor-style cut that suits live wood. It is a solid all-round hand pruner for structural pruning on young trees and for cleaning up cuts aloft.
highlights: Bypass action for clean cuts on live wood
Cuts branches up to 1 in. thick
Good for young-tree structural pruning
Durable everyday hand pruner
Keep it sharp for the cleanest cuts

p: A bypass pruner works like scissors: the sharp blade passes the hook so the cut is clean on the side left on the tree. That matters on live wood, where a crushed stub heals slower. Anvil pruners crush more and are better kept for dead material.

A 1 in. capacity covers most small cuts when training young trees, clearing sprouts and making final cuts back to a branch collar. For anything larger, a hand saw makes a cleaner cut than forcing the pruner.

A good pair of hand pruners is one of the most used tools in the kit, both on the ground and aloft. Climbers doing fine pruning often prefer pruners to a saw for the smallest cuts, since they are quicker and give a cleaner finish on thin wood.

Cut with the blade on the side of the branch that stays on the tree, just outside the branch collar. Keep the blade sharp with a small stone, wipe sap off after use and oil the pivot. Wear gloves and eye protection. If you carry it aloft, use a holster on the saddle so it is secure. See more in our pruners and loppers section.
Replacement blades and springs keep a good pruner going for years, so check whether parts are available for your model before tossing a worn one.

faq.q: Bypass or anvil pruner for trees?
faq.a: Bypass for live wood, since it gives a cleaner cut. Anvil pruners are better for dry, dead material.

faq.q: Can it cut a branch bigger than 1 in.?
faq.a: Do not force it. Use a hand saw for larger branches to avoid damaging the pruner and the tree.
